summary.headline: Waaree RTL Q2 FY27 revenue rose 36.53% YoY to INR1,057.84 crore, but EBITDA margin fell to 15.12% as solar EPC execution dropped to 456 MWp.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue from operations for Q2 FY27 was INR1,057.84 crore, up 36.53% YoY, with EBITDA of INR159.98 crore (15.12% margin) and PAT of INR81.48 crore. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,982.09 crore (+43.84%), with EBITDA of INR333.46 crore (16.82%) and PAT of INR200.44 crore. This quarter was the first full consolidation of Associated Power Structures (APSPL), the T&D subsidiary, which added debt-funded acquisition finance costs and depreciation. Solar EPC execution slowed to 456 MWp in Q2 from about 889-922 MW in earlier comparison periods, which management attributed to land and connectivity handover delays on the developer side; 1.7 GW of new orders were booked in the quarter.

segments.name: Solar EPC
segments.commentary: Executed 456 MWp in Q2 FY27 and 1,345 MWp in H1 FY27. Management says solar EPC should remain the key growth driver and expects margin above 15%.

segments.name: T&D (APSPL)
segments.commentary: Consolidated from Q2 FY27; margin currently about 9-10%, below solar EPC. Management said FY26 revenue was close to INR2,000 crore and the order book is INR2,200 crore plus as of Q2; order pipeline above INR20,000 crore.

segments.name: IPP and O&M
segments.commentary: Operational IPP portfolio is 82.82 MWp; O&M portfolio has reached 1.5 GWp, which management says adds recurring revenue.

segments.name: BESS EPC
segments.commentary: Management cites rising inquiries to add BESS to existing solar plants and in new orders; no BESS revenue or margin figures given.

guidance_outlook: Unexecuted consolidated order book above INR5,500 crore as of 30 Sep 2026 (EPC solar and BESS above INR3,300 crore; T&D above INR2,200 crore), to be executed over the next 3-4 quarters.
Solar EPC EBITDA margin expected to stay above 15%, per management's estimate.
T&D margin expected to improve from 9-10% as scale and synergies with Waaree Renewables and APSPL build; visibility expected from the coming quarter.
Interest and depreciation expected to stabilise over time; management aims to reduce interest cost and debt over coming quarters.
Management did not give a FY27 revenue or execution target. It cited FY26 revenue of about INR3,300 crore as the base.
capex_capacity: Solar EPC execution: 456 MWp in Q2 FY27; 1,345 MWp in H1 FY27.
Order inflow: about 1.7 GWp of new orders in Q2 FY27 from a mix of existing and new customers.
Additional T&D manufacturing facility at Azamnagar with 1 lakh metric tons capacity, under expansion.
Operational IPP portfolio 82.82 MWp; O&M portfolio 1.5 GWp.
demand_pricing: Management says India had about 299 GW of renewable capacity and about 171 GW of solar as of 30 Sep 2026; India added about 44 GW of solar last year and over 20 GW in H1 FY27.
Solar EPC domestic and international pipeline cited at about 25 GW domestic and 9 GW international, with some references to a 30-35 GW total pipeline.
BESS: CEA estimates about 208 GWh requirement by 2030; about 144 GWh of BESS above 1 MWh tracked as of May 2026, of which about 7.5 GWh commissioned.
Green Energy Corridor Phase 3 approved with about INR1.86 lakh crore outlay, targeting 135 GW RE evacuation and 50 GWh BESS by FY32-33.

Management says the majority of solar orders are utility scale and that most customers are repeat group companies via bilateral discussions. No pricing or realisation figures were disclosed despite analyst questions.

qa_highlights.question: Why did solar execution fall to about 456 MW in Q2 versus about 889-922 MW earlier, and what is the FY27 target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited land and connectivity handover delays at the developer end on some projects, which it said are customer-side. Projects will be executed over the next 3-4 quarters. No FY27 execution target was given.

qa_highlights.question: Why are T&D margins lower and when will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: T&D margin is currently about 9-10%, below solar EPC. Management expects improvement in coming quarters from scale, efficiency and synergies with Waaree Renewables and APSPL.

qa_highlights.question: Why did finance cost and depreciation rise sharply, and when will APSPL offset them?
qa_highlights.answer: Depreciation is mostly from the acquisition. Finance cost rose because the acquisition was debt-funded. Management said APSPL's contribution should cover the loan over time, without a date.

qa_highlights.question: Is the debt level permanent?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the loan was taken for the APSPL acquisition and it will look to reduce debt as operations progress. No target leverage level was given.

qa_highlights.question: Are there working capital, bank guarantee, or NFB constraints on bidding?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there are no constraints; limits are available for new bids. No specific limit amounts were disclosed.

risks_watch: Solar EPC execution reliance on developers' land and grid connectivity readiness; the Q2 slowdown was attributed to this.
Margin dilution from the lower-margin T&D business (9-10%) and higher debt-related finance cost and depreciation after the APSPL acquisition.
Q2 PAT down about 30% YoY as cited by analyst, despite 36.53% revenue growth; management did not dispute the figure.

Order conversion: INR5,500 crore order book depends on developer readiness and conversion over 3-4 quarters; the solar EPC book of INR3,300 crore is smaller than the INR5,300-crore book cited in the prior call.
Consolidated debt level and the pace of its reduction; the company did not give a repayment timeline.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order visibility, but evasive on specifics. Management repeatedly declined to quantify execution targets, realisations, order-level delays, T&D mix or timelines for debt reduction, and it answered several questions only in general terms.
